name: gradio-rag-llm
description: A start-GREEN Gradio chatbot that does retrieval-augmented generation over a REAL pgvector sibling AND calls a REAL model (OpenAI-compatible endpoint) to generate the grounded answer, appending a code-produced [id] citation. Deterministic stdlib-embedding retrieval keeps the verifiable contract reproducible; the LLM supplies the prose. Exercises the model endpoint (and the opt-in key-proxy) from inside the sandbox.
interface: core.generate_reply(message: str, history: list | None = None) -> str
knowledge:
This PoC GENERATES its answer with a REAL LLM call but appends the citation in CODE, so the DETERMINISTIC, verifiable part of a reply is the `[id]` citation marker — NOT the model's free-form prose (which varies run to run). The scaffold ships `core.CORPUS` (a FIXED list of docs, each {id, title, content}; you CANNOT add facts), deterministic `retrieve`/`snippet`/`cite` (`cite` → `[<int id>]`, e.g. `[1]`, ids are INTEGERS), AND `_answer(question, context)` (the real model call). `generate_reply` should: retrieve the doc, call the LLM to answer from that doc's content, then append `cite(doc)`. The corpus covers retrieval-augmented generation, pgvector similarity search, grounded citations, and the Gradio chat interface; an unrelated query (e.g. 'weather on Mars') matches nothing and yields the no-match reply.
TO TEST DETERMINISTICALLY (the LLM's wording is NON-deterministic — NEVER assert exact sentences or a fixed phrase the model must produce): `from core import CORPUS`; for an in-corpus query (words from a doc's title) assert the reply contains a `[N]` marker whose integer N matches a CORPUS doc id (read the integer between the brackets, match `next(d for d in CORPUS if d['id'] == int(N))`), AND that the reply is NON-TRIVIAL (longer than the bare marker — i.e. the model actually generated an answer). For an unrelated query, assert the reply contains NO `[N]` marker (the no-match path). For discrimination, assert two different in-corpus topics cite DIFFERENT ids. Do NOT assume a `[doc-N]`/`[source:title]` format, and do NOT assert the model's exact text — only structure (citation presence/absence, the integer id match, non-trivial length).
